newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair says rocking days are definitely over.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair says rocking days are definitely over.

text.p: British opposition leader Tony Blair, fighting to win a May 1 election, on Tuesday made a campaign pledge not even his rivals can criticise -- he promised never to play in a rock band again.
The leader of the Labour party issued his promise after a young man asked him what he would do about Britain's massively successful rock music industry if he took power.
Blair, once the lead singer of a short-lived rock group called 'Ugly Rumours' while at university, replied: "I'll tell you what I'm going to do about British rock music.
"I'm not going to play in a band again."
Blair's vow of musical silence is likely to be welcomed by the ruling Conservatives, who polls make underdogs for the election after 18 years in power without a break.
Conservative officials have been angered by the prospect of Labour getting free publicity and additional campaign funds from another pop song -- its campaign anthem.
Blair has chosen the 1994 chart-topping song "Things Can Only Get Better" by the group D:Ream as the theme tune for his bid to dislodge Prime Minister John Major.
D:Ream lead singer Peter Cunnah has agreed to re-issue the song and give all royalties to Labour's fighting fund.
Conservative officials have called on the BBC, which is governed by tough rules during the campaign to ensure a lack of bias, to boycott the song.
But the BBC has said that if the song makes the national top 40, it will have to play it on its chart shows.
The Labour-backing Daily Mirror newspaper called on readers to buy a copy as soon as it hit the shops next Monday to ensure it shoots up to the top of the charts.
